name: FinBERT + GDELT news sentiment with XGBoost for FX and bonds

origin.source_title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Macro Alpha: A News Sentiment Case Study (arXiv 2505.16136)

how_it_works.simple: A finance-trained language model reads world news every day and scores how positive or negative it is. A second model uses those scores to guess whether the euro or yen will go up or down tomorrow.
how_it_works.analogy: Like guessing tomorrow's mood in a classroom by reading today's school newsletter.
how_it_works.precise: Score GDELT articles with FinBERT, aggregate into daily indices of mean tone, dispersion and event impact, add lags (1 to 3 days) and 5 and 20 day moving averages plus technical features, and train an XGBoost classifier for next-day direction of EUR/USD, USD/JPY and 10-year Treasury futures with expanding-window cross-validation.

rule: At each day t close, build sentiment features from articles available up to t, predict P(up) for day t+1 with XGBoost, go long if P(up) > 0.5 and short otherwise, paying 0.02 percent per round trip on FX.
data_needed: GDELT event and article tone data (free, 15-minute updates)
economic_rationale: News tone and disagreement may carry macro information that FX prices absorb slowly, per the author.
why_it_might_fail: A daily FX Sharpe near 6 would beat every known macro fund by a wide margin, which points to leakage or overfitting. GDELT timestamps are UTC while FX closes at 5pm New York, so articles after the close can enter day t features. Logistic regression on the same features gives Sharpe 0.66 to 0.83, so most of the result comes from the flexible model.

reported_results.notes: Read on the arXiv HTML page. Win rate 72.7 percent. USD/JPY Sharpe 4.65, CAGR 53.2 percent, max drawdown -22.9 percent; ZN Sharpe 4.65, CAGR 22.1 percent. Very likely too good to be true: single author, no independent replication, hyperparameters tuned within the cross-validation scheme, and a possible close-time mismatch. The linked code repository returned 404 when checked.
USD/JPY logistic Sharpe 0.66, CAGR 6.2 percent; ZN -0.15. The more plausible range for a daily news signal.

post_publication_evidence: No independent replication or live results found. The code link in the paper (github.com/yukepenn/macro-news-sentiment-trading) returned 404 on 2026-10-20.

implementations.notes: FinBERT model used for sentiment scoring.

relevance.reason: Directly targets FX with free data and is easy to replicate, which makes it a good leakage test case even if the headline numbers are not believable.
